newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Trygg-Hansa says nees more cost cutting.
newsitem.headline: Trygg-Hansa says nees more cost cutting.

text.p: Swedish insurer Trygg-Hansa AB said on Friday that continued cost cuts were needed due to increasing competition in the insurance sector.
Posting a slight rise in its nine-month profit to 2,101 million crowns from 2,088 million, the company said it was aiming for lower prices and simpler products.
"In addition we are actively investing in the growing areas of life insurances, savings and welfare," Trygg-Hansa said in a statement.
"Once again a fine result," said chief executive Lars Thunell in the statement.
"However in view of mounting competition in the industry, continued cost reductions are necessary.
"This will enable us to increase our competitive strength through a continued movement toward lower rates and simpler products."

He said the process of change being carried out by Trygg-Hansa was having an increasingly strong impact on the company's results, despite continued competition in the Swedish non-life insurance market.
For the nine months, Trygg-Hansa said net premiums earned in the non-life areas decreased to 3.76 billion crowns from 4.06 billion a year ago.
This was due mainly to lower earned premiums for accepted reinsurance, the termination of cooperation with Sampo and the sales of Hansa Industrial Insurance, the company said.
Claims incurred decreased to 3.17 billion crowns from 3.44 billion with a net loss ratio of 84.2 percent against 84.8 percent.
On the technical account non-life business totalled 583 million versus 479 million a year ago.
"Following a review of risk selection based on claims statistics, actions taken in the commercial traffic operations have quickly led to measurable improvement," the company said.
The balance on the technical account for life insurance was a loss of 25 million crowns against zero a year ago.

"Taken into account the surplus values that continuously arise in the unit-linked operations, (i.e., embedded value), the life insurance operations show a positive trend in results," the statement said.
Operating expenses in the nine months fell to 872 million crowns against 994 million a year ago.
The net expense ratio decreased to 23.2 percent against 24.5 percent a year ago.
